The Ashram

A Sanctuary in the Deccan

Mallayyagiri is not only a place of worship. It is a home for seekers, a kitchen that never closes, and a living reminder that the sacred can be found in ordinary service.

Founded in 2006

Where Sadhana Became a Home

In 2006, after years of pilgrimage and penance, Sri Dr. Basavalinga Avadhoota settled at Mallayyagiri, a quiet stretch of land between Kuppanagar and Chillapalli. What began as a simple place of worship has become an ashram with a shrine, a satsang hall, a kitchen and room for the thousands who arrive on Pournami.

The ashram belongs to no one person. It is cared for by devotees who cook, clean, garden, sing and sit together. On any given day you might find a farmer, a student, a doctor and a grandmother sharing the same prasada — which is exactly the point.

A second ashram at Degalmadi in Kalburgi district carries the same rhythm of worship and service into Karnataka.

The Daily Rhythm

A Day at the Ashram

The ashram moves with the sun and the seasons. These are the rhythms that shape an ordinary day — festival days are fuller, quieter days are just as sacred.

Early morning

Suprabhata & abhisheka

The shrine opens with prayer, abhisheka and a period of quiet meditation before the day's work begins.

01
Morning

Seva & ashram life

Devotees and residents tend the gardens, prepare the kitchen and look after the daily needs of the ashram.

02
Midday

Annadanam

Prasada is served to all who arrive. Visitors are welcome to join the meal and the seva that makes it possible.

03
Evening

Satsang & bhajan

Gurudev's discourses, devotional singing and quiet reflection draw the day to a close.

04
Night

Aarti & silence

The final aarti is offered, lamps are lit, and the ashram settles into the silence that gives it its character.

05

Timings shift with the season, the festival calendar and Gurudev's travel. Please call the ashram office before travelling if you are coming for a specific programme.

Getting here

Nearest town: Jharasangam. Nearest city: Zaheerabad. Please call ahead for route guidance, local transport and accommodation. The ashram office can help you plan the last leg of your journey.

Before You Come

Visitor Guidance

The ashram is a place of worship and a family home. A little care helps everyone feel welcome.

  • Dress modestly and comfortably. Traditional Indian clothing is appreciated but not required.
  • Remove footwear before entering the shrine and satsang hall.
  • Please ask before photographing the shrine, the Guru or other devotees.
  • Keep conversation low in the meditation areas and switch phones to silent.
  • Alcohol, tobacco and non-vegetarian food are not permitted on the ashram grounds.
  • Accommodation and prasada are offered as seva; call ahead so the ashram can prepare for you.

For accommodation, group visits and festival arrangements, please call +91 63052 90187 or email basavalingavadhoot@gmail.com.
